countObserved: 978 passed, exit 0 — reproduced independently in my own worktree at 2330e9c with `python3 -m pytest scripts/ plugins/*/skills/*/tests/ plugins/*/skills/*/scripts/ -q > file 2>&1; echo $?` (unpiped $?). Agrees with the fix report. Targeted file: 16 passed. Baseline pytest here is 9.1.1, pyyaml 6.0.1, markdown-it-py 4.2.0, jsonschema 4.26.0.

defects.summary: The pip-install recogniser anchors on the command STARTING with pip/python -m pip, so any wrapper token in front hides a drifted pin completely — and the "second pair of eyes" stray-scalar test shares the same recogniser, so nothing catches it. The file's central promise ("FAIL-CLOSED IS THE POINT... not a silent pass") is false.
defects.evidence:
PIP_INSTALL (scripts/test_workflow_dependency_pins.py:61-65) requires the match to sit at start-of-string or right after one of [\n;&|(], with only an optional `python|python3 [-opts] -m ` prefix. Nothing may sit between `pip` and `install` either. I replaced ci.yml's pytest-windows install line with each of the following and ran `python3 -m pytest scripts/test_workflow_dependency_pins.py -q` (all restored afterwards; `git status` clean):
  rc=0 `sudo python3 -m pip install pyyaml==6.0.1`
  rc=0 `env FOO=1 pip install pyyaml==6.0.1`
  rc=0 `uv pip install pyyaml==6.0.1`
  rc=0 `$PY -m pip install pyyaml==6.0.1`
  rc=0 `python3 -m pip -q install pytest pyyaml==6.0.1 markdown-it-py==4.2.0 jsonschema==4.26.0`
Each drops from 16 to 14 passed (the two parametrized checks for that install simply stop being generated) and exits 0. For the last one — a drifted pyyaml pin AND an unpinned pytest, i.e. exactly the pre-change state the branch exists to prevent — I also ran the real gate: `python3 -m pytest scripts/ -q` → exit 0, "581 passed". `pip <global-opt> install` is documented pip usage and `sudo`/`$PY` prefixes are ordinary. The vacuous-pass guard only fires when EVERY install is hidden (verified: hiding all of them gives "1 failed, 5 passed, 2 skipped"); partial drift is silent. This also falsifies requirements-dev.txt:6-8 ("asserts that every `pip install` in every workflow installs THIS FILE") and the docstring's "a FAILURE naming the file and line" — workflow failures name file/job/step index, never a line. Contrast: `--quiet`, `pip3 install`, `python -m pip install`, `\`-continuations, `if`-blocks and heredoc bodies are all correctly RED, so the fix is narrowing the anchor, not rebuilding the walk.

defects.summary: `-c/--constraint` is deliberately consumed as a value option, so a constraints file — which silently overrides every pin in requirements-dev.txt — passes green, defeating the "ONLY place a version is written down" claim the test exists to hold.
defects.evidence: VALUE_OPTIONS at scripts/test_workflow_dependency_pins.py:79-87 includes "-c" and "--constraint", and install_operands() skips their value (line 191-192). Measured: replacing ci.yml's pytest-windows install with `python3 -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt -c constraints.txt` → rc=0, "16 passed". A constraints file is functionally a second pin file — `pyyaml==6.0.1` in constraints.txt beats `pyyaml==6.0.3` in requirements-dev.txt — which is precisely the "second place a version is written down" that test_a_workflow_install_reads_the_declared_requirements_file rejects for a second `-r`. `-r` is validated against REQUIREMENTS; `-c` should be too (or rejected outright). Same measurement for `--index-url https://evil.example.com/simple` → rc=0, which redirects every declared pin to another index without a test noticing.

defects.summary: requirements-dev.txt's header asserts "every entry here is a pure-Python wheel" — false for PyYAML, and nothing checks it. This is the exact #120 shape: an unverifiable claim load-bearing in the design argument for installing the whole set everywhere.
defects.evidence: requirements-dev.txt:16-18: "every entry here / is a pure-Python wheel, so the extra install is cheap next to the checkouts / and clones these jobs already do." PyPI, queried this session: pyyaml 6.0.3 publishes 73 files and ZERO `py3-none-any` wheels — every wheel is a cp3XX platform wheel (`pyyaml-6.0.3-cp310-cp310-manylinux2014_aarch64...whl` etc.), because PyYAML builds the libyaml C extension. markdown-it-py 4.2.0 and jsonschema 4.26.0 do ship pure wheels; jsonschema also pulls `rpds-py`, a Rust extension, transitively. The sentence is the whole cost argument for the whole-set decision, so a reader who checks it finds the argument's premise wrong. The pre-rewrite wording ("The four are pure-Python wheels", commit 2330e9c) was equally false — the cleanup commit generalised it rather than checking it.

defects.summary: Two added comments assert that no two of the old inline pip lines named the same package subset. Checkably false from the very diff that removes them — ci.yml's `pytest` and `pytest-windows` lines were byte-identical, and the comment this change deletes said so in as many words.
defects.evidence: requirements-dev.txt:4-6 "the same pins were restated inline in every workflow job that needed them, each naming a different subset"; scripts/test_workflow_dependency_pins.py:5-7 "restated once per job, and no two of those lines named the same subset". At the base commit b81f6f1, `git show b81f6f1:.github/workflows/ci.yml | grep -n 'pip install'` gives line 271 and line 357 both as `python3 -m pip install pytest pyyaml==6.0.3 markdown-it-py==4.2.0 jsonschema==4.26.0` — identical. The deleted comment at ci.yml:264-266 read "Pins are deliberately IDENTICAL to the consistency and skills-conformance jobs above". "restated once per job" is also wrong: account-skill-zips' `zip` job, ci.yml's `plugin-validate` and `shellcheck`, and every job in record-account-upload.yml and scheduled-run-health.yml had no install. Commit 2330e9c introduced both sentences while removing counts, i.e. it traded a true count for a false universal.

defects.summary: The vacuous-pass guard's docstring claims deleting every install makes "the rest of this file go quiet" — measured, five other tests still run and pass, and the last test's own docstring says the opposite.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_workflow_dependency_pins.py:204-205: "Every assertion below is over the installs found; delete them all and the rest of this file goes quiet." I rewrote every workflow install as `sudo python3 -m pip install ...` (hiding all of them) and got "1 failed, 5 passed, 2 skipped": the four parametrized test_no_pip_install_hides_where_the_parsed_walk_cannot_see_it cases and test_every_declared_requirement_is_pinned_exactly all still ran. test_every_declared_requirement_is_pinned_exactly's own docstring (line 326-328) explicitly says it exists to run "even on a day when no workflow names a package", directly contradicting the guard's claim.

defects.summary: test_every_declared_requirement_is_pinned_exactly's failure message asserts it catches extras; it does not. A requirement with an extra passes.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_workflow_dependency_pins.py:331-334 asserts on the version half only and says "An environment marker, extra or URL here would make what CI installs depend on the runner." Appending `pytest-cov[toml]==7.0.0` to requirements-dev.txt → rc=0, "16 passed": canonical() leaves `pytest-cov[toml]` intact as the name and `7.0.0` satisfies the version regex. The marker case (`requests==2.32.3 ; python_version < "3.13"`) and the bare/range/duplicate/recursive-`-r` cases do all correctly RED — extras are the one member of the message's own list that slips through, so the message names a guarantee the code does not give.

defects.summary: A package declared in requirements-dev.txt that nothing in the repo imports is never flagged, and no comment carves that out — while the docstring's "covered the moment it is added" reads as though it were.
defects.evidence: Appending `requests==2.32.3` to requirements-dev.txt → rc=0, "16 passed", and the full `scripts/` suite stays green. Since every job now installs the whole set, a stale entry costs install time in five jobs and is invisible. scripts/test_workflow_dependency_pins.py:18-19 says "a package added to requirements-dev.txt is covered the moment it is added, and nothing here has to be widened to notice it" — true only in the workflow-side direction; nothing checks the file-side direction, and neither the docstring nor the requirements header says so.

defects.summary: Composite actions under .github/actions/**/action.yml are ungoverned and the stated scope carve-out does not mention them, so the omission reads as unconsidered rather than decided.
defects.evidence: workflow_files() (scripts/test_workflow_dependency_pins.py:126-127) globs .github/workflows/*.yml|*.yaml only. I created .github/actions/setup/action.yml containing a composite step `python3 -m pip install pyyaml==6.0.1` → rc=0, "16 passed" (removed afterwards). The scope paragraph at lines 37-40 justifies the boundary solely by the shipped skill asset (plugins/adam/skills/github-actions-repo-settings/assets/workflows/), which is a real and correct carve-out; composite actions are a different, in-repo surface a future change would naturally add, and the fix report records them only in its own stillOpen notes, not in the repo. Per AGENTS.md durable findings belong in the repo.
